Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, third quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, Head of Investor Relations.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's third quarter results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Jordan. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid third quarter, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover our overall financial performance, the factors impacting gross margins including commodity costs, pricing, and mix; our price elasticity observations; the pricing actions we've taken and their impact on sales; marketing campaign effectiveness; and competitive activity along with our responses. These elements underscore our ability to drive growth and efficiency in the CPG landscape.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Mike Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $4.2 billion, representing a 5% increase compared to the prior year. Gross margin was 41.8%, driven by a balanced mix of commodity cost management, strategic pricing, and favorable product mix. Operating income was $450 million. Diluted earnings per share were $0.85. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me expand on these results, starting with the key drivers behind our gross margin performance, which expanded 240 basis points year-over-year and 110 basis points sequentially to 41.8%. This is our strongest quarterly expansion in three years, achieved through proactive strategies across commodity costs, pricing, and mix in a volatile input environment similar to the 2022 spikes in cocoa and palm oil.

On commodity costs, we faced an 80 basis point headwind, largely offset by hedging and procurement. Cocoa surged 28% year-over-year to $4,200 per metric ton due to West African disruptions, adding $45 million to COGS, much like challenges for Hershey and Mondelez. Palm oil rose 15% sequentially from El Niño effects in Indonesia and Malaysia, contributing $30 million, while sugar and corn derivatives increased 12% tied to Brazilian supply shifts. Our 18-month rolling hedge covered 75% of cocoa needs at 20% below spot, saving $25 million. Multi-year contracts with suppliers like Barry Callebaut and Wilmar included ESG clauses to mitigate risks. North America saw milder 10% inflation versus 22% in EMEA, and APAC benefited from local sourcing cutting transport by 8%. For Q4, we anticipate 50-60 basis point headwinds as hedges roll off, stress-testing for cocoa at $5,000.

Pricing provided a 320 basis point tailwind with 7.5% average increases across the portfolio, realizing 92% versus our 85-90% target, thanks to premium segment resilience. Snacks like NovaCrunch bars took 9% hikes in North America with -0.3 elasticity versus -0.6 for mass peers. Beverages saw 8% on functional drinks, household care 6% to defend against P&G. LatAm hit +11% amid inflation, EMEA +5% with EDLP. No major competitive rollbacks from private labels, and trade spend efficiency down 150 basis points to 22% amplified gains. We see 4-5% runway into FY25, monitoring IRI and Nielsen basket trends.

Mix added 100 basis points, with premium health products at 38% of sales up from 32%, driving 250 basis points accretion. Plant-based snacks grew 22% at 52% margins versus 38% for legacy. Rationalized 15% low-margin SKUs, exiting $120 million revenue, while coffee pods rose 18%. North America mix up 140 basis points, APAC 80 basis points. Our Focus 15 initiative prunes 5,000+ SKUs, invests in low-sugar reformulations, and uses SymphonyAI for 200 basis points more lift.

Net, gross profit dollars up 9% to $2.8 billion despite flat volumes. Q4 guide: 42.0-42.5%, with 95% on-time delivery and $150 million spec-out savings.

Turning to price elasticity observations, which underpin our pricing discipline amid 22% COGS inflation offset by 18% cumulative pricing. Portfolio elasticity averaged -0.45 this quarter, better than -0.75 in Q4 2022, via PeakPricing Analytics integrating IRI, Kroger/Albertsons loyalty, and our 15 million household database for SKU-store-week testing.

Beauty/personal care at -0.32: Olay-like serum up 12% ASP held volumes via penetration to 27%. Snacks more elastic at -0.68: Crunch bars -4.1% units countered by pack shrinks and premium variants up 8% share. North America -0.41 with EDLP at Target/Costco, trade spend to 18%. Europe -0.52, leaning mid-tier bundles. LatAm -0.39, APAC ex-China -0.71 with dynamic pilots.

Our framework: 150+ quarterly experiments at 85% approval, $250 million trade reallocation, monitoring trade-down. Expect -0.4 to -0.5 into FY25, supporting 4-5% pricing, 2% volume growth, 650 basis points YTD margin to 48.2%.

On pricing actions and sales impact, they drove 4.2% organic growth: +5.8 points pricing offset -1.1% volume. Snacks/confectionery (28% revenue): 7-9% on CrunchBar/NutriTrail, +8.2% realization, 6.1% sales despite -2% volume, trade to 18%. Beverages (35%): +3.5% cautious, flat sales via dynamic shelf pricing up 3% conversion. Household/personal: +4.1%, +2.5% volume.

North America +6.5%, 5.8% growth. Europe +4.2%, 3.1%. EM +7.8%, 4.9%. Pricing Excellence 2.0 cuts leakage to 1.4%, +70 basis points margin. Q4 +4-5%, 15 premium SKUs.

Finally, competitive activity: Intense with private labels at 28% NMV. North America: Kraft Heinz +12% trade, private labels 32% laundry; we EDLP FreshWash, sustainability for +7% premium share, Amazon +15%. Europe: Reckitt €150M campaign +3.2 points, Unilever +1.5; EuroVital 12 SKUs, +1,200 facings to 92% ACV. EM: Dabur +4 points, FEMSA pressure; VitalRoots 8% share, precision farming reversed losses.

Globally +2.8% realization, +110 basis points margin. CPG 3.0 tech preempts moves. H2 spend to 22%, 2-3% growth with 200 basis points share.

With that strong financial foundation, I will now turn the call over to Lisa Patel to discuss marketing and brand performance.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Mike. We saw strong performance in our Refresh Beverages and Glow Essentials brands this quarter. Diving into marketing campaign effectiveness, a cornerstone of our A&P spend at $525 million, up 8% year-over-year but flat at 12.5% of sales. In CPG's thin-margin, shelf-competitive world amid softening sentiment and inflation, precision marketing exceeded hurdles with 4.7x blended ROAS, up from 3.9x, above 3.5x benchmarks per Nielsen/IRI.

MMM and MTA via GCB Insights showed $2.47 billion sales lift, +22% YoY, 5.2 MER, CAC down 15% to $28, CLV up 11% to $450, repeats to 68%. Digital 62% budget at 5.8x ROAS vs. 3.2x traditional; reallocated $45 million from TV. Shopper marketing +14% basket incidence, +9% AOV to $42 with Walmart/Kroger/Tesco.

Refresh Revolution for sparkling waters: $120 million CTV/social/events, 7.1x ROAS, +28% share in $15B NA functional, 62% causal lift. Empower Everyday for Glow skincare: 6.4x ROAS, 22% conversion at $65 AOV. Planet Positive eco-packaging: +18 favorability to 76%, +12% volume.

Regions: NA 5.3x with Walmart Connect +25% households; EMEA 3.9x countered Amazon/Carrefour; APAC 5.1x China KOLs/India JioMart +35%/19%.

Tech: AI demand sensing 92% accuracy, UID 2.0 -40% signal loss, DCO +23% CTRs, RCTs.

Doubling omnichannel, total shopper equity against private labels +2.3 points. ESG +15% ROI. Q4/FY24 4.8-5.2x ROAS, $2.2B A&P for 5-7% growth, gen AI pilots, APAC DTC. Risks FX/recession, but data agility.

Our recent Refresh Revolution campaign has resonated well with consumers. We are also excited about the launch of our new Planet Positive eco-packaging cleaners, which is already generating positive feedback and driving volume growth.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for submitting questions will now be provided. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the details of the new marketing campaign and its impact on sales?

Lisa Patel:
Good morning, John. The Refresh Revolution campaign for our low-sugar sparkling waters invested $120 million across CTV, TikTok, Instagram Reels, and experiential events, delivering 7.1x ROAS and a 28% market share gain in the North American functional beverage segment. Incrementality tests confirmed 62% causal sales lift of over $800 million, without cannibalizing our soda lines, directly contributing to our overall 5% sales growth and strengthening brand equity against competitors like LaCroix.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for addressing rising commodity costs in the coming quarters?

Mike Chen:
Thanks, Emily. We're well-hedged with 75% coverage on key inputs like cocoa at 20% below spot, saving $25 million this quarter, and multi-year ESG-linked contracts with suppliers like Barry Callebaut and Wilmar. For Q4, headwinds moderate to 50-60 basis points as La Niña eases palm oil, but we're stress-testing cocoa to $5,000 with regional sourcing in APAC and value engineering for $150 million savings. This supports our 42-42.5% margin guide while maintaining supply resilience at 95% on-time delivery.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley.

David Lee:
How is the current inflationary environment impacting consumer demand for your premium product lines?

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, David. Inflation has tested demand, but our premium lines at 38% of sales show resilience, with inelasticity around -0.32 in beauty and plant-based snacks growing 22% in volume at higher margins. Pricing realization at 92% and campaigns like Planet Positive lifting favorability 18 points have sustained household penetration, offsetting trade-down via superior quality perception and omnichannel shopper equity.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays.

Rachel Kim:
Can you discuss the performance of your e-commerce channel this quarter?

Lisa Patel:
Hi Rachel. E-commerce was a standout, with 35% penetration in EM via Tmall/JD.com and JioMart driving 35% YoY growth in APAC, and Amazon ACV up 15% in NA nutrition bars via dynamic pricing for 18% higher baskets. Digital A&P at 62% budget yielded 5.8x ROAS, Shopify/Amazon personalization converting 22% at $65 AOV in beauty, and Walmart Connect integrations capturing 25% more households—key to our 5.2 MER and overall sales lift.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders, with ROAS guidance of 4.8-5.2x, continued margin expansion, and 2-3% organic growth. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. third quarter Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
